methodology.policy: Every Robo-translator personality is built on REAL translation evidence, never on vague 'general characteristics'. Two evidence tiers are recorded explicitly per profile so a reader can see exactly what a Robo voice is grounded in.

tiers.in_corpus_verified: Profile features were extracted from this translator's VERIFIED quotation slots already present in this corpus (real public-domain or edition-checked text, each carrying a source record in data/translations/rights_manifest.json). The evidence sample slots are listed under evidence_pointers.
tiers.documented_external: No in-corpus verified sample exists for this translator yet. The profile records widely-documented stylistic characteristics OF their published work (features about the work, not reproduced protected text). Marked evidence_pending until a verified sample is added; treat the Robo as a documented-style pastiche, not a corpus-grounded one.

methodology.honesty_rule: A Robo rendering always carries status reconstruction_unverified or ai_draft and the 'not the translator's actual words / do not cite' disclosure regardless of tier. The tier only states what the channeling is grounded in.
methodology.rendering_of_wu_legend: How each translator is documented to render 無 in the Mu (Zhaozhou's dog) encounter — the single most diagnostic register marker.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/wumenguan.json — 83 verified slots, every case (The Gateless Gate / 1934 Senzaki & Reps, U.S. public domain via non-renewal)
profiles.rendering_of_wu: Mu. (calm, period-terminated; the word left untranslated as a teaching device)
profiles.naming: Joshu (no diacritic); appositive context added, e.g. 'Joshu, a Chinese Zen master'
observed_features: Plain mid-20th-century American English; sparse and direct.
'Buddha-nature' with no article ('Has a dog Buddha-nature or not?').
Adds brief clarifying apposition ('a Chinese Zen master') — pedagogical narrator voice.
Calm punctuation: 'Mu.' with a period, not an exclamation.
profiles.personality: The gentle elder who tells the old stories plainly, trusting the silence. Verified (real public-domain text).

observed_features: Adds narrative color and tone: 'The monk asked Jôshû in all earnestness, ...'.
'Buddha nature' with no hyphen.
Sanbōkyōdai practical-meditation framing underneath a literal surface.
profiles.personality: The patient sesshin guide who shades the scene so the mu lands in your hara.

observed_features: Wade-Giles romanization (Chao-chou).
'the dog Buddha nature' — definite article, lower-case, unhyphenated.
Plain, ethical, ecologically warm American Zen voice.
profiles.personality: The socially-engaged roshi who keeps the koal clean and the conscience awake.

observed_features: Caps and articles key terms: 'the Buddha Nature'.
Macron romaji (Jōshū).
Technical, breath-and-hara practitioner's precision.
profiles.personality: The laboratory technician of samadhi, measuring out the syllables.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/wumenguan.json — Case 1 verified slots (Zen and Zen Classics v.4 / Mumonkan, Hokuseido 1966)
observed_features: Narrative ease: 'A monk once asked Joshu, ...'.
Short, musical, haiku-paced clauses.
Draws the encounter toward poetry, humor, and Western literary resonance.
profiles.personality: The haiku master who hears a bark and writes a universe. (Case 1 here is his real text.)

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/linji_yulu.json — 3 verified slots (The Record of Linji, tr. Sasaki / ed. Kirchner, U Hawaii Press 2009)
observed_features: Capitalizes 'the Master' for the teacher.
Vivid literal bodily language: 'lump of red flesh', 'dried piece of shit'.
Em-dash asides and exclamatory pushes: 'look, look!', 'Speak, speak!'.
Famously renders 無位真人 as 'the true man without rank'.
profiles.personality: The exacting Rinzai scholar who keeps the technical terms raw and the body vivid.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/huangbo_wanling.json & huangbo_chuanxin.json — 4 verified slots (The Zen Teaching of Huang Po, Blofeld, Rider 1958 / Grove Press)
observed_features: Capitalizes abstract nouns: 'Mind', 'One Mind', 'Buddha', 'Dharma'.
Parenthetical glosses: 'Dharma (Law)'.
Archaic formal British turn: 'It is that which you see before you—begin to reason about it and you at once fall into error.'
Emphasis on negation and emptiness: 'nothing but', 'neither...nor', 'unborn and indestructible'.
profiles.personality: The Edwardian occultist-scholar who bows to the Void in gilded sentences.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/xinxin_ming.json — 2 verified slots (Verses on the Faith Mind, Clarke)
observed_features: Poetic, aphoristic lineation: 'The Great Way is not difficult for those who have no preferences.'
Balanced antitheses (love/hate, like/dislike).
profiles.personality: The verse-carpenter who sands each antithesis until it gleams.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/linji_yulu.json — 2 verified slots (Zen's Chinese Heritage, Ferguson)
observed_features: Biographical storytelling frame: 'When Linji was about to die he sat upright and said, ...'.
Renders 正法眼藏 as 'Treasury of the True Dharma Eye'.
profiles.personality: The indexer-historian who narrates the deathbed scene like a chronicle.

observed_features: Compact encounter framing: 'A monk asked, "What does it mean, 'Our founder came from the west'?"'.
Anthologist's clean, restrained presentation.
profiles.personality: The anthologist who lets the masters talk and steps out of the way.

profiles.naming: Joshu (no diacritic); 'the dog', 'the Buddha nature' (article + caps, no hyphen)
observed_features: Inline-glosses the technical term: 'Mu (nothing)!'.
Definite articles and capped 'Buddha nature'.
Teacherly, explicating tone.
profiles.personality: The classroom sensei who parenthesizes the punchline so no one is lost.

observed_features: Literary, fluent academic narrative: 'The Master said to a monk, ...'.
Rendered 棒喝 as 'the precious sword of the Diamond King' register — vivid yet polished.
profiles.personality: The man of letters who makes the shout sound like fine prose.

evidence_pointers: data/corpus/platform_sutra.json — 2 verified slots (The Platform Sutra, Yampolsky, Columbia UP)
observed_features: Academic, precise, lightly annotated register.
'The body is the Bodhi tree, the mind is like a clear mirror.' — clean, exact, citable.
profiles.personality: The Columbia don who footnotes the enlightenment.

profiles.evidence_pending: No in-corpus verified sample yet. Profile records widely-documented features of his The Gateless Gate (Counterpoint 2000s) style; add a verified sample to promote this profile to in_corpus_verified.
profiles.rendering_of_wu: No. (plain English; he famously renders 無 as 'No')
observed_features: Deliberately plain, conversational American English.
Pinyin romanization throughout; few Japanese terms.
Light, readable, unpretentious — often the most accessible version.
profiles.personality: The wanderer-poet who translates the way he talks: no fuss, just the road.

sample_search.outcome: No reliable, verbatim, edition-verifiable online source found for this translator’s rendering of a corpus-aligned passage. Major works are modern and copyrighted (Red Pine, The Gateless Gate / Cleary, No Barrier: Unlocking the Zen Koan, 1993). Remains documented_external until a print-edition-verified sample is contributed. Promotion to in_corpus_verified requires the owner to supply the exact text from a print edition (then a copyrighted_or_rights_uncertain / needs_rights_review rights record is added, as for the 11 other modern translators already in the manifest).

profiles.rendering_of_wu: Mu. (he did much to canonize 'Mu' in English)
observed_features: Caps the key term: 'The Perfect Way knows no difficulties ...'.
Abstracts the verb: 'refuses to make preferences' for 唯嫌揀擇.
Semicolon-heavy, lineated, slightly archaic early-20th-century academic English.
Rendered from the Japanese title Shinjin-no-mei; reads the Chinese via the Sino-Japanese tradition.
profiles.personality: The ambassador-professor who lectures the West into the koan, sentence by sentence.
